question: What the scripts are handed for the null tag's country, and what the spare manpower reads after entering.

addresses.name: CCountryTag::GetCountry
addresses.comment: **The tag -> country lookup the whole image goes through: 1295 direct call sites.** Five instructions, no branch, no call: `g_CCountryDataBase->countries_first[this->id]`. `mov eax,[ecx]` reads the four tag characters and `mov [esp],eax` stores them in a stack slot nothing reads again - the dead half of a by-value CCountryTag copy the optimiser flattened - so only `this->id` at +4 is used. It does not range-check the id and it does not check that g_CCountryDataBase is non-null. **So the null tag (id 0) answers the placeholder country `---`**, the first of the list, never nothing - and a script is handed it: Their Finest Hour's JAP.lua asks the leader of the misspelt faction "cominterm" (the null tag, CFaction::GetFactionLeader with no members) for its country and that for a relation, which has no war (FINDINGS-liveread.md section 108).
addresses.evidence: Japan's foreign minister on the running game after a load of Ireland1941_07_16_07 made all six of ForeignMinister_Tick's rolls at 19:00 (probes/hoiluawhere.lua: ai_foreign_minister.lua lines 81-116) after its war roll took JAP.lua's ForeignMinister_ProposeWar through line 699, loCominternCountry:GetRelation(loAxisTag), without an error.
addresses.revises: comment - the null tag answers the placeholder country, which scripts are handed

struct_fields.name: starting_manpower
struct_fields.comment: LoadKey copies Manpower into this the moment it has read the `manpower` key. **Its real meaning is the second writer's, and the name does not fit it**: CCountry::UpdateManpowerAfterMobilising (0xDCD70), run every day in RunCountryDailyPass and after every unit order, sets it to the manpower pool plus half a year's manpower before its multipliers, less the men every reinforcing brigade lacks plus a quarter of each one's build manpower, less the built-strength men of each brigade of a reserve line. Its reader is the Lua `HasExtraManpowerLeft` (rva 0x4E81E0, `> 0`). The name is kept because BiceLib's CCountry.hpp uses it; `spare_manpower` is what it is. **Made on entering a loaded game too** (CInGameIdler::Enter's call): read on the running game after a load of Ireland1941_07_16_07, Germany 1009.971, Japan 899.791, Yugoslavia 2.768, Bulgaria -7.968 - so the production script's first day after a load builds units for Yugoslavia and none for Bulgaria (FINDINGS-liveread.md section 108).
struct_fields.evidence: readInteger(country + 0x158) for GER, JAP, BUL and YUG on the game standing at 21:00 on 16 July 1941, after entering; Bulgaria's production minister took the no-units branch of ProductionMinister_Tick (BuildOtherUnits at line 1107) and Yugoslavia's the other (lines 1091 and 1098).
struct_fields.revises: comment - made on entering as well, and figures read
